title: Human gestures tend to follow Menzerath’s law
text:
Here we check the null model that is used at the end of the analysis pages. The simulated data has the same structure as our dataset (corpora, speakers, number of gestures), and follows the preprocessing: peaks are at least 160 ms apart, n_sub is the number of intervals between peaks, and a gesture needs at least one interval.
Code
library(data.table)
library(lmerTest)
set.seed(2137)

# figures in the html at 300 dpi
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dpi = 300, fig.retina = 1)

# minimum time between peaks in seconds (PEAK_DIST = 4 frames at 25 fps in the preprocessing)
min_gap <- 0.16

title: Human gestures tend to follow Menzerath’s law
text:
Simulated data
With b = 0, nothing links submovement duration to the number of submovements. With b < 0, gestures with more submovements are sped up, i.e., a real Menzerath effect.


Code
make_data <- function(b = 0, gap = min_gap) {
  n_spk  <- c(ECOLANG = 15, MULTISIMO = 18, GESres = 7, SAGA = 4, SAGAplus = 10, ZHUBO = 1)
  n_gest <- c(ECOLANG = 3718, MULTISIMO = 1188, GESres = 1029, SAGA = 687, SAGAplus = 675, ZHUBO = 86)
  g <- rbindlist(lapply(names(n_spk), function(cc) {
    rate <- rlnorm(n_spk[cc], log(2.5), 0.15)              # peaks per second, per speaker
    s <- sample(n_spk[cc], n_gest[cc], replace = TRUE)
    data.table(corpus = cc, speaker = paste0(cc, "_", s), rate = rate[s])
  }))
  g[, `:=`(gid = seq_len(.N), dur = rlnorm(.N, log(1.4), 0.5))]
  g[, {
    t <- cumsum(gap + rexp(ceiling(dur / gap) + 2, 1 / (1 / rate - gap)))
    t <- t - runif(1) * t[1]
    iv <- diff(t[t <= dur])
    if (length(iv) >= 1) {
      f <- (length(iv) / 4)^b
      list(sub_dur = iv * f, gesture_dur = dur * f, n_sub = length(iv))
    }
  }, by = .(corpus, speaker, gid)]
}

# the same model as on the analysis pages:
# x = number of submovements within speaker, xb = speaker mean, by-speaker random slopes, corpus as fixed effect
add_predictors <- function(d) {
  d <- copy(d)
  d[, spk := paste(corpus, speaker)]
  d[, lx := log(n_sub)]
  # speaker means are taken over gestures
  d[, m := mean(lx[!duplicated(gid)]), by = spk]
  d[, x := (lx - m) / sd(d$lx)]
  d[, xb := (m - mean(d$lx)) / sd(d$lx)]
  d[, y := scale(log(sub_dur))[, 1]]
  d
}

paper_model <- function(d) {
  lmer(y ~ x + xb + corpus + (1 + x | spk) + (1 | gid), data = add_predictors(d),
       control = lmerControl(calc.derivs = FALSE))
}

d0 <- make_data(b = 0)
d1 <- make_data(b = -0.1)

Per-corpus slopes (as in the analysis pages), data without an effect


Code
per_corpus <- function(d) {
  d <- add_predictors(d)
  # one model with a within-speaker slope for each corpus
  mod <- lmer(y ~ 0 + corpus + corpus:x + xb + (1 + x | spk) + (1 | gid), data = d)
  cf <- coef(summary(mod))
  rows <- grep(":x$", rownames(cf), value = TRUE)
  out <- data.table(corpus = sub("^corpus", "", sub(":x$", "", rows)),
                    beta = cf[rows, "Estimate"], p = cf[rows, "Pr(>|t|)"])
  out[d[, .(gestures = uniqueN(gid)), by = corpus], on = "corpus", gestures := i.gestures]
  out[, singular := isSingular(mod)]
  out
}

n_removed <- length(unique(fulldat$event_id[n_rows != fulldat$n_submovements]))

fulldat$event_id <- as.factor(fulldat$event_id)
fulldat$corpus <- as.factor(fulldat$corpus)
fulldat$speaker <- as.factor(fulldat$speaker)
fulldat$subtype <- as.factor(fulldat$subtype)
fulldat$condition <- as.factor(fulldat$condition)

# speakers get an id that is unique over corpora
fulldat$speaker_id <- as.factor(paste(fulldat$corpus, fulldat$speaker))

# gesture category only
gesdat <- subset(fulldat, condition == "gesture")
gesdat$corpus <- droplevels(gesdat$corpus)
gesdat$speaker <- droplevels(gesdat$speaker)
gesdat$gesture_id <- droplevels(gesdat$gesture_id)

# objman category only
objman_dat <- subset(fulldat, condition == "objman")
objman_dat$corpus <- droplevels(objman_dat$corpus)
objman_dat$speaker <- droplevels(objman_dat$speaker)
objman_dat$gesture_id <- droplevels(objman_dat$gesture_id)

# means and SDs of the log-transformed variables, i.e., what scale(log()) does in the models
# we need these to draw the model lines and to get the unscaled exponent
get_scaling <- function(data) {
  list(mx = mean(log(data$n_submovements)), sx = sd(log(data$n_submovements)),
       my = mean(log(data$subm_dur_ms)),    sy = sd(log(data$subm_dur_ms)))
}
sc_ges <- get_scaling(gesdat)
sc_obj <- get_scaling(objman_dat)

# the number of submovements is one value per gesture, so its slope compares gestures with each other
# we split the (log) number of submovements in a part within speaker and a part between speakers:
# x_between = the mean of the speaker, x_within = the deviation of a gesture from the mean of its speaker
# both are divided by the same SD, so x_within + x_between is the scale(log(n_submovements)) of before
add_predictors <- function(data, group = "speaker_id", trans = log, names = c("x_within", "x_between")) {
  x <- trans(data$n_submovements)
  # speaker means are taken over gestures (one value per gesture), not over submovements
  one <- !duplicated(data$event_id)
  speaker_mean <- tapply(x[one], as.character(data[[group]][one]), mean)
  m <- as.numeric(speaker_mean[as.character(data[[group]])])
  data[[names[1]]] <- (x - m) / sd(x)
  data[[names[2]]] <- (m - mean(x)) / sd(x)
  data
}
gesdat <- add_predictors(gesdat)
objman_dat <- add_predictors(objman_dat)

title: Human gestures tend to follow Menzerath’s law
text:
Here we run the two Python scripts that turn the skeleton files (Mediapipe world landmarks, 25 fps) into the submovement datasets that are analyzed on the next pages. Both scripts do the same thing, and only differ in how a speed peak is defined.

Peak method 1: a peak is a local maximum in the index finger speed of the dominant hand that is above 0.15 m/s (15 cm/s).
Peak method 2: a peak is a local maximum that is above 10% of the maximum speed of that gesture.

In both methods the positions are smoothed with a Gaussian filter (SD = 2 frames, 80 ms), the speed is smoothed once more, and peaks need to be at least 4 frames (160 ms) apart. A submovement is the interval between two consecutive peaks, so the number of submovements is the number of peaks minus one. Gestures with fewer than two peaks have no interval, they are flagged as single_unit and are excluded in the analyses.






NoteCode for running the Python scripts







Code
# Use this conditional approach:
if (rstudioapi::isAvailable()) {
  # Running in RStudio
  current_dir <- dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path)
} else {
  # Running outside RStudio (like command line quarto)
  current_dir <- here::here()
}

# settings
rerun <- FALSE                      # set to TRUE to force a rerun of both scripts
python_exe <- Sys.which("python")   # change this if your python lives somewhere else
if (python_exe == "") python_exe <- Sys.which("python3")

script_dir <- paste0(current_dir, "/Code_Processing/PeakExtractionCode")
output_dir <- paste0(current_dir, "/Data_Output")

# runs one script and returns what it printed
run_method <- function(method) {
  script  <- paste0("processingGestures_method", method, ".py")
  outfile <- paste0(output_dir, "/gestures_long_method", method, ".csv")
  flatfile <- paste0(output_dir, "/gestures_flat_method", method, ".csv")
  logfile <- paste0(output_dir, "/processing_log_method", method, ".txt")

  # we only run when the output is missing or older than the script
  stale <- !file.exists(outfile) || !file.exists(flatfile) || !file.exists(logfile) ||
    file.mtime(outfile) < file.mtime(paste0(script_dir, "/", script))

  if (rerun || stale) {
    # the scripts use relative paths (../../Data_Input), so we run them from their own folder
    old_dir <- setwd(script_dir)
    on.exit(setwd(old_dir))
    errfile <- tempfile()
    log <- system2(python_exe, script, stdout = TRUE, stderr = errfile)
    if (!is.null(attr(log, "status"))) {
      stop(paste(c(paste(script, "failed:"), tail(readLines(errfile), 20)), collapse = "\n"))
    }
    # the script should have written both datasets
    if (!file.exists(outfile) || !file.exists(flatfile)) {
      stop(paste(c(paste0(script, " ran, but did not write gestures_flat_method", method, ".csv and gestures_long_method", method, 
                          ".csv in Data_Output. Is this the latest version of the script? Its output was:"), 
                   tail(log, 15)), collapse = "\n"))
    }
    writeLines(log, logfile)
  }
  readLines(logfile)
}

log_method1 <- run_method(1)
log_method2 <- run_method(2)






Peak method 1 (absolute threshold)






NotePython code: processingGestures_method1.py





"""
Gesture Submovement Analysis (peak method 1: absolute speed threshold)
Processes NPZ skeleton files (mediapipe world landmarks) to extract submovement metrics.
Peaks are local maxima in index finger speed above 0.15 m/s that are at least 160 ms apart.
A submovement is the interval between two consecutive peaks.
"""

import os
import hashlib
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from tqdm import tqdm

# landmark indices in 23-landmark upper body array
LM = {
    "left_shoulder": 11, "right_shoulder": 12,
    "left_elbow": 13, "right_elbow": 14,
    "left_wrist": 15, "right_wrist": 16,
    "left_index": 19, "right_index": 20
}

# parameters
SPEED_THRESH = 0.15  # m/s (15 cm/s), absolute threshold for movement and for peaks
SIGMA = 2            # gaussian sd in frames (2 frames = 80 ms at 25 fps)
PEAK_DIST = 4        # min distance between peaks in frames (4 frames = 160 ms at 25 fps)
FPS = 25


def get_xyz(world, idx):
    # world shape: (frames, 92), each landmark = 4 values (x,y,z,vis)
    return world[:, idx*4 : idx*4+3]


def get_speed(pos, ts):
    # smooth position per axis and compute 3D speed (m/s)
    smooth = np.column_stack([gaussian_filter1d(pos[:,i], SIGMA) for i in range(3)])
    dt = np.diff(ts)
    dt[dt == 0] = 1/FPS  # guard against duplicate timestamps
    vel = np.diff(smooth, axis=0) / dt[:, None]
    speed = np.sqrt((vel**2).sum(axis=1))
    # diff loses one frame, so repeat the first speed value
    # (padding with 0 gives a fake peak when the hand already moves at clip start)
    speed = np.concatenate([[speed[0]], speed])
    # smooth the speed once more
    return gaussian_filter1d(speed, SIGMA)


def get_path_length(pos):
    # total distance travelled (m) of the smoothed position
    smooth = np.column_stack([gaussian_filter1d(pos[:,i], SIGMA) for i in range(3)])
    return np.sqrt((np.diff(smooth, axis=0)**2).sum(axis=1)).sum()


def parse_filename(fpath):
    # parse: CORPUS_speaker_clipid_gesture_subtype_skeleton.npz
    fname = os.path.basename(fpath).replace("_skeleton.npz", "")
    parts = fname.split("_")

    # find gesture index
    gidx = next((i for i,p in enumerate(parts) if p.lower() == "gesture"), None)
    if gidx is None or gidx < 2:
        return None

    # clip id sits right before "gesture", speaker is everything between corpus and clip id
    corpus = parts[0]
    clip_id = parts[gidx - 1]
    speaker = "_".join(parts[1:gidx-1]) if gidx > 2 else parts[1]
    subtype = parts[gidx + 1] if gidx + 1 < len(parts) else "NA"

    # ZHUBO single speaker
    if corpus == "ZHUBO":
        speaker = "zhubo"

    return {"corpus": corpus, "speaker": speaker, "clip_id": clip_id, "subtype": subtype}


def process_file(fpath):
    # parse metadata
    meta = parse_filename(fpath)
    if meta is None:
        return None, None, None

    # condition from folder
    condition = "objman" if "objman" in fpath.lower() else "gesture"

    # load npz
    data = np.load(fpath, allow_pickle=True)

    # find world landmarks array (shape n x 92)
    world = None
    for k in data.files:
        if isinstance(data[k], np.ndarray) and data[k].ndim == 2 and data[k].shape[1] == 92:
            world = data[k]
            break
    if world is None or len(world) < 3:
        return None, None, None

    # fingerprint of the skeleton data, used to find files with exactly the same data
    data_key = hashlib.md5(np.ascontiguousarray(np.round(world, 6) + 0.0).tobytes()).hexdigest()
    
    # timestamps (in seconds), fall back on frame number / fps
    ts = data["timestamps"] if "timestamps" in data.files else np.arange(len(world)) / FPS

    # extract positions
    left_idx = get_xyz(world, LM["left_index"])
    right_idx = get_xyz(world, LM["right_index"])

    # path lengths
    left_path = get_path_length(left_idx)
    right_path = get_path_length(right_idx)

    # handedness based on whether movement threshold is reached
    left_speed = get_speed(left_idx, ts)
    right_speed = get_speed(right_idx, ts)
    left_moves = left_speed.max() >= SPEED_THRESH
    right_moves = right_speed.max() >= SPEED_THRESH

    if left_moves and right_moves:
        hand = "bimanual"
    elif left_moves:
        hand = "left"
    elif right_moves:
        hand = "right"
    else:
        hand = "none"

    # dominant side = the hand with the longest path, all further analysis is on this side
    if left_path >= right_path:
        dom = "left"
        idx_pos = left_idx
        wrist_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["left_wrist"])
        elbow_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["left_elbow"])
        shoulder_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["left_shoulder"])
    else:
        dom = "right"
        idx_pos = right_idx
        wrist_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["right_wrist"])
        elbow_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["right_elbow"])
        shoulder_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["right_shoulder"])

    # speeds
    speed_idx = get_speed(idx_pos, ts)
    speed_wrist = get_speed(wrist_pos, ts)
    speed_elbow = get_speed(elbow_pos, ts)
    speed_shoulder = get_speed(shoulder_pos, ts)

    # peaks = local maxima above the speed threshold and at least PEAK_DIST frames apart
    # index finger peaks define the submovements, the other joints are only counted
    peaks_idx, _ = find_peaks(speed_idx, distance=PEAK_DIST, height=SPEED_THRESH)
    peaks_wrist, _ = find_peaks(speed_wrist, distance=PEAK_DIST, height=SPEED_THRESH)
    peaks_elbow, _ = find_peaks(speed_elbow, distance=PEAK_DIST, height=SPEED_THRESH)
    peaks_shoulder, _ = find_peaks(speed_shoulder, distance=PEAK_DIST, height=SPEED_THRESH)

    # metrics
    dur_ms = (ts[-1] - ts[0]) * 1000
    n_peaks = len(peaks_idx)
    # a submovement is the interval between two peaks, so number of intervals is one less than number of peaks
    n_subm = max(n_peaks - 1, 0)
    # single unit = fewer than two peaks, so there is no interval (these are excluded in the analysis)
    single_unit = 1 if n_peaks <= 1 else 0

    if n_peaks > 1:

        intervals = np.diff(peak_times) * 1000
        mean_subm_dur = intervals.mean()
    else:
        # no interval, so we fall back on the whole gesture duration
        mean_subm_dur = dur_ms

    # id used as random intercept in the models
    # we use the file name, as corpus_speaker_clipid is not unique in MULTISIMO and SAGA
    gid = os.path.basename(fpath).replace("_skeleton.npz", "")

    # flat row (one row per gesture)
    flat = {

        "speaker": meta["speaker"],
        "clip_id": meta["clip_id"],
        "subtype": meta["subtype"],
        "condition": condition,
        "duration_ms": dur_ms,

        "n_submovements": n_subm,
        "single_unit": single_unit,
        "handedness": hand,
        "dominant_side": dom,
        "path_left": left_path,
        "path_right": right_path,
        "path_dominant": get_path_length(idx_pos),
        "max_speed": speed_idx.max(),
        "n_peaks_index": len(peaks_idx),
        "n_peaks_wrist": len(peaks_wrist),
        "n_peaks_elbow": len(peaks_elbow),
        "n_peaks_shoulder": len(peaks_shoulder)
    }

    # long rows - base info shared across submovements (same n_submovements as in flat)
    base = {
        "gesture_id": gid,
        "corpus": meta["corpus"],
        "speaker": meta["speaker"],
        "clip_id": meta["clip_id"],

        "n_peaks_elbow": len(peaks_elbow),
        "n_peaks_shoulder": len(peaks_shoulder)
    }

    long_rows = []
    if n_peaks > 1:
        # one row per submovement, running from peak i to peak i+1
        peak_times = np.sort(ts[peaks_idx])
        for i in range(len(peak_times) - 1):
            row = base.copy()
            row.update({
                "subm_index": i + 1,
                "subm_dur_ms": (peak_times[i+1] - peak_times[i]) * 1000,
                "peak_time_ms": peak_times[i] * 1000,
                "peak_speed": speed_idx[peaks_idx[i]]
            })
            long_rows.append(row)
    else:
        # single unit: one placeholder row with the whole gesture duration (n_submovements = 0)
        row = base.copy()
        row.update({
            "subm_index": 1,
            "subm_dur_ms": dur_ms,
            "peak_time_ms": ts[peaks_idx[0]] * 1000 if len(peaks_idx) > 0 else dur_ms / 2,
            "peak_speed": speed_idx.max()
        })
        long_rows.append(row)

    return flat, long_rows, data_key

"""
Gesture Submovement Analysis (peak method 2: relative speed threshold)
Processes NPZ skeleton files (mediapipe world landmarks) to extract submovement metrics.
Peaks are local maxima in index finger speed above 10% of the max speed of that gesture, at least 160 ms apart.
A submovement is the interval between two consecutive peaks.
"""

import os
import hashlib
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from tqdm import tqdm

# landmark indices in 23-landmark upper body array
LM = {
    "left_shoulder": 11, "right_shoulder": 12,
    "left_elbow": 13, "right_elbow": 14,
    "left_wrist": 15, "right_wrist": 16,
    "left_index": 19, "right_index": 20
}

# parameters
SIGMA = 2                 # gaussian sd in frames (2 frames = 80 ms at 25 fps)
PEAK_DIST = 4             # min distance between peaks in frames (4 frames = 160 ms at 25 fps)
FPS = 25
PEAK_HEIGHT_RATIO = 0.10  # 10% of max speed
MOVE_THRESH = 0.15        # m/s (15 cm/s), only used for handedness (same as method 1)


def get_xyz(world, idx):
    # world shape: (frames, 92), each landmark = 4 values (x,y,z,vis)
    return world[:, idx*4 : idx*4+3]


def get_speed(pos, ts):
    # smooth position per axis and compute 3D speed (m/s)
    smooth = np.column_stack([gaussian_filter1d(pos[:,i], SIGMA) for i in range(3)])
    dt = np.diff(ts)
    dt[dt == 0] = 1/FPS  # guard against duplicate timestamps
    vel = np.diff(smooth, axis=0) / dt[:, None]
    speed = np.sqrt((vel**2).sum(axis=1))
    # diff loses one frame, so repeat the first speed value
    # (padding with 0 gives a fake peak when the hand already moves at clip start)
    speed = np.concatenate([[speed[0]], speed])
    # smooth the speed once more
    return gaussian_filter1d(speed, SIGMA)


def get_path_length(pos):
    # total distance travelled (m) of the smoothed position
    smooth = np.column_stack([gaussian_filter1d(pos[:,i], SIGMA) for i in range(3)])
    return np.sqrt((np.diff(smooth, axis=0)**2).sum(axis=1)).sum()


def parse_filename(fpath):
    # parse: CORPUS_speaker_clipid_gesture_subtype_skeleton.npz
    fname = os.path.basename(fpath).replace("_skeleton.npz", "")
    parts = fname.split("_")

    # find gesture index
    gidx = next((i for i,p in enumerate(parts) if p.lower() == "gesture"), None)
    if gidx is None or gidx < 2:
        return None

    # clip id sits right before "gesture", speaker is everything between corpus and clip id
    corpus = parts[0]
    clip_id = parts[gidx - 1]
    speaker = "_".join(parts[1:gidx-1]) if gidx > 2 else parts[1]
    subtype = parts[gidx + 1] if gidx + 1 < len(parts) else "NA"

    # ZHUBO single speaker
    if corpus == "ZHUBO":
        speaker = "zhubo"

    return {"corpus": corpus, "speaker": speaker, "clip_id": clip_id, "subtype": subtype}


def process_file(fpath):
    # parse metadata
    meta = parse_filename(fpath)
    if meta is None:
        return None, None, None

    # condition from folder
    condition = "objman" if "objman" in fpath.lower() else "gesture"

    # load npz
    data = np.load(fpath, allow_pickle=True)

    # find world landmarks array (shape n x 92)
    world = None
    for k in data.files:
        if isinstance(data[k], np.ndarray) and data[k].ndim == 2 and data[k].shape[1] == 92:
            world = data[k]
            break
    if world is None or len(world) < 3:
        return None, None, None

    # fingerprint of the skeleton data, used to find files with exactly the same data
    data_key = hashlib.md5(np.ascontiguousarray(np.round(world, 6) + 0.0).tobytes()).hexdigest()
    
    # timestamps (in seconds), fall back on frame number / fps
    ts = data["timestamps"] if "timestamps" in data.files else np.arange(len(world)) / FPS

    # extract positions
    left_idx = get_xyz(world, LM["left_index"])
    right_idx = get_xyz(world, LM["right_index"])

    # path lengths
    left_path = get_path_length(left_idx)
    right_path = get_path_length(right_idx)

    # handedness based on whether the absolute movement threshold is reached
    # (10% of the max over both hands is reached by almost any hand, so everything would be bimanual)
    left_speed = get_speed(left_idx, ts)
    right_speed = get_speed(right_idx, ts)
    left_moves = left_speed.max() >= MOVE_THRESH
    right_moves = right_speed.max() >= MOVE_THRESH

    if left_moves and right_moves:
        hand = "bimanual"
    elif left_moves:
        hand = "left"
    elif right_moves:
        hand = "right"
    else:
        hand = "none"

    # dominant side = the hand with the longest path, all further analysis is on this side
    if left_path >= right_path:
        dom = "left"
        idx_pos = left_idx
        wrist_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["left_wrist"])
        elbow_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["left_elbow"])
        shoulder_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["left_shoulder"])
    else:
        dom = "right"
        idx_pos = right_idx
        wrist_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["right_wrist"])
        elbow_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["right_elbow"])
        shoulder_pos = get_xyz(world, LM["right_shoulder"])

    # speeds
    speed_idx = get_speed(idx_pos, ts)
    speed_wrist = get_speed(wrist_pos, ts)
    speed_elbow = get_speed(elbow_pos, ts)
    speed_shoulder = get_speed(shoulder_pos, ts)

    # peak threshold is 10% of max speed
    # note: there is no absolute floor here, so tracking jitter of a still hand also gives peaks
    # (max_speed is saved, so these can be filtered in the analysis)
    peak_thresh = speed_idx.max() * PEAK_HEIGHT_RATIO

    # peaks = local maxima above the relative threshold and at least PEAK_DIST frames apart
    # index finger peaks define the submovements, the other joints are only counted (each with its own max)
    peaks_idx, _ = find_peaks(speed_idx, distance=PEAK_DIST, height=peak_thresh)
    peaks_wrist, _ = find_peaks(speed_wrist, distance=PEAK_DIST, height=speed_wrist.max() * PEAK_HEIGHT_RATIO)
    peaks_elbow, _ = find_peaks(speed_elbow, distance=PEAK_DIST, height=speed_elbow.max() * PEAK_HEIGHT_RATIO)
    peaks_shoulder, _ = find_peaks(speed_shoulder, distance=PEAK_DIST, height=speed_shoulder.max() * PEAK_HEIGHT_RATIO)

    # metrics
    dur_ms = (ts[-1] - ts[0]) * 1000
    n_peaks = len(peaks_idx)
    # a submovement is the interval between two peaks, so number of intervals is one less than number of peaks
    n_subm = max(n_peaks - 1, 0)
    # single unit = fewer than two peaks, so there is no interval (these are excluded in the analysis)
    single_unit = 1 if n_peaks <= 1 else 0

    if n_peaks > 1:
        peak_times = np.sort(ts[peaks_idx])
        intervals = np.diff(peak_times) * 1000
        mean_subm_dur = intervals.mean()
    else:
        # no interval, so we fall back on the whole gesture duration
        mean_subm_dur = dur_ms

    # id used as random intercept in the models
    # we use the file name, as corpus_speaker_clipid is not unique in MULTISIMO and SAGA
    gid = os.path.basename(fpath).replace("_skeleton.npz", "")

    # flat row (one row per gesture)
    flat = {
        "gesture_id": gid,
        "corpus": meta["corpus"],
        "speaker": meta["speaker"],
        "clip_id": meta["clip_id"],
        "subtype": meta["subtype"],
        "condition": condition,
        "duration_ms": dur_ms,
        "mean_subm_dur_ms": mean_subm_dur,
        "n_submovements": n_subm,
        "single_unit": single_unit,
        "handedness": hand,
        "dominant_side": dom,
        "path_left": left_path,
        "path_right": right_path,
        "path_dominant": get_path_length(idx_pos),
        "max_speed": speed_idx.max(),
        "n_peaks_index": len(peaks_idx),
        "n_peaks_wrist": len(peaks_wrist),
        "n_peaks_elbow": len(peaks_elbow),
        "n_peaks_shoulder": len(peaks_shoulder)
    }

    # long rows - base info shared across submovements (same n_submovements as in flat)
    base = {
        "gesture_id": gid,
        "corpus": meta["corpus"],
        "speaker": meta["speaker"],
        "clip_id": meta["clip_id"],
        "subtype": meta["subtype"],
        "condition": condition,
        "duration_ms": dur_ms,
        "n_submovements": n_subm,
        "single_unit": single_unit,
        "handedness": hand,
        "dominant_side": dom,
        "path_left": left_path,
        "path_right": right_path,
        "path_dominant": get_path_length(idx_pos),
        "max_speed": speed_idx.max(),
        "n_peaks_index": len(peaks_idx),
        "n_peaks_wrist": len(peaks_wrist),
        "n_peaks_elbow": len(peaks_elbow),
        "n_peaks_shoulder": len(peaks_shoulder)
    }

    long_rows = []
    if n_peaks > 1:
        # one row per submovement, running from peak i to peak i+1
        peak_times = np.sort(ts[peaks_idx])
        for i in range(len(peak_times) - 1):
            row = base.copy()
            row.update({
                "subm_index": i + 1,
                "subm_dur_ms": (peak_times[i+1] - peak_times[i]) * 1000,
                "peak_time_ms": peak_times[i] * 1000,
                "peak_speed": speed_idx[peaks_idx[i]]
            })
            long_rows.append(row)
    else:
        # single unit: one placeholder row with the whole gesture duration (n_submovements = 0)
        row = base.copy()
        row.update({
            "subm_index": 1,
            "subm_dur_ms": dur_ms,
            "peak_time_ms": ts[peaks_idx[0]] * 1000 if len(peaks_idx) > 0 else dur_ms / 2,
            "peak_speed": speed_idx.max()
        })
        long_rows.append(row)

    return flat, long_rows, data_key


# main
input_dirs = ["../../Data_Input/Gesture", "../../Data_Input/Objman"]
output_dir = "../../Data_Output"

# collect files
npz_files = []
for d in input_dirs:

    if flat:

        if data_key in seen:

            continue
        seen[data_key] = os.path.basename(fpath)
        flat_rows.append(flat)
        long_rows.extend(longs)

# save (flat = one row per gesture, long = one row per submovement)
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
df_flat = pd.DataFrame(flat_rows)
df_long = pd.DataFrame(long_rows)

df_flat.to_csv(f"{output_dir}/gestures_flat_method2.csv", index=False)

df_removed = pd.DataFrame(removed, columns=["removed", "kept"])
df_removed.to_csv(f"{output_dir}/duplicates_removed_method2.csv", index=False)

    print(f"\nCondition counts:\n{df_flat['condition'].value_counts()}")
    print(f"\nSingle units (excluded in analysis): {df_flat['single_unit'].sum()}")
    
    # numbers for reporting: speakers and gestures per corpus (after removing duplicates)
    counts = df_flat.groupby(["condition", "corpus"]).agg(
        n_speakers=("speaker", "nunique"),
        n_gestures=("gesture_id", "count"),
        n_in_analysis=("single_unit", lambda s: int((s == 0).sum())))
    print("\nSpeakers and gestures per corpus:")
    for (cond, corp), r in counts.iterrows():
        print(f"  n speakers = {r['n_speakers']}, n gestures = {r['n_gestures']} ({r['n_in_analysis']} in analysis), {corp} [{cond}]")
    for cond, r in counts.groupby(level="condition").sum().iterrows():
        print(f"  total [{cond}]: n gestures = {r['n_gestures']} ({r['n_in_analysis']} in analysis)")

    # gesture ids are the random intercepts, so they should be unique per event
    n_dup = df_flat["gesture_id"].duplicated().sum()
    if n_dup > 0:
        print(f"\nWarning: {n_dup} duplicated gesture ids")

title: Human gestures tend to follow Menzerath’s law

NoteCode for dataset loading, plotting defaults







We load the submovement dataframe of peak method 2 (see the preprocessing page).


Code
library(cowplot)
library(ggplot2)

# figures in the html at 300 dpi (saved figures are 600 dpi)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dpi = 300, fig.retina = 1)

# Use this conditional approach:
if (rstudioapi::isAvailable()) {
  # Running in RStudio
  current_dir <- dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path)
} else {
  # Running outside RStudio (like command line quarto)
  current_dir <- here::here()
}

# load full data (one row per submovement) for this peak method
datafile <- paste0(current_dir, "/Data_Output/gestures_long_method", method, ".csv")
fulldat <- read.csv(datafile)

# events with fewer than two peaks have no interval between peaks, so no submovement duration
fulldat <- subset(fulldat, single_unit == 0)

# check: the number of rows of an event should equal its number of submovements
# (if not, a gesture id is not unique and we remove those events)
fulldat$event_id <- paste(fulldat$condition, fulldat$gesture_id)
n_rows <- table(fulldat$event_id)[fulldat$event_id]
n_removed <- length(unique(fulldat$event_id[n_rows != fulldat$n_submovements]))
fulldat <- fulldat[n_rows == fulldat$n_submovements, ]

fulldat$gesture_id <- as.factor(fulldat$gesture_id)
fulldat$event_id <- as.factor(fulldat$event_id)
fulldat$corpus <- as.factor(fulldat$corpus)
fulldat$speaker <- as.factor(fulldat$speaker)
fulldat$subtype <- as.factor(fulldat$subtype)
fulldat$condition <- as.factor(fulldat$condition)

# speakers get an id that is unique over corpora
fulldat$speaker_id <- as.factor(paste(fulldat$corpus, fulldat$speaker))

# gesture category only
gesdat <- subset(fulldat, condition == "gesture")
gesdat$corpus <- droplevels(gesdat$corpus)
gesdat$speaker <- droplevels(gesdat$speaker)
gesdat$gesture_id <- droplevels(gesdat$gesture_id)

# objman category only
objman_dat <- subset(fulldat, condition == "objman")
objman_dat$corpus <- droplevels(objman_dat$corpus)
objman_dat$speaker <- droplevels(objman_dat$speaker)
objman_dat$gesture_id <- droplevels(objman_dat$gesture_id)

# means and SDs of the log-transformed variables, i.e., what scale(log()) does in the models
# we need these to draw the model lines and to get the unscaled exponent
get_scaling <- function(data) {
  list(mx = mean(log(data$n_submovements)), sx = sd(log(data$n_submovements)),
       my = mean(log(data$subm_dur_ms)),    sy = sd(log(data$subm_dur_ms)))
}
sc_ges <- get_scaling(gesdat)
sc_obj <- get_scaling(objman_dat)

# the number of submovements is one value per gesture, so its slope compares gestures with each other
# we split the (log) number of submovements in a part within speaker and a part between speakers:
# x_between = the mean of the speaker, x_within = the deviation of a gesture from the mean of its speaker
# both are divided by the same SD, so x_within + x_between is the scale(log(n_submovements)) of before
add_predictors <- function(data, group = "speaker_id", trans = log, names = c("x_within", "x_between")) {
  x <- trans(data$n_submovements)
  # speaker means are taken over gestures (one value per gesture), not over submovements
  one <- !duplicated(data$event_id)
  speaker_mean <- tapply(x[one], as.character(data[[group]][one]), mean)
  m <- as.numeric(speaker_mean[as.character(data[[group]])])
  data[[names[1]]] <- (x - m) / sd(x)
  data[[names[2]]] <- (m - mean(x)) / sd(x)
  data
}
gesdat <- add_predictors(gesdat)
objman_dat <- add_predictors(objman_dat)
